subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own the Agentic OS lease/session RPC contract and its persisted state, or should core expose only a generic authorization/metadata seam for an external owner integration?
rationale: This choice determines the public Gateway API, persistence ownership, upgrade contract, and long-term compatibility burden; it cannot be resolved safely as a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Use a generic core seam
options.body: Keep core limited to generic host-validated spawn authorization and metadata hooks, with the Agentic OS methods and policy owned by its integration.

options.title: Sponsor the core contract
options.body: Explicitly accept the seven Gateway methods and persisted snapshot behavior as supported core API, then require protocol, migration, and real-runtime upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Close or defer the PR if no owner is prepared to support this external contract as either a plugin integration or a core API.

recommendation.title: Use a generic core seam
recommendation.body: Keep core limited to generic host-validated spawn authorization and metadata hooks, with the Agentic OS methods and policy owned by its integration.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the proposed contract and can supply the intended integration boundary while a core owner makes the final product decision.
